title: The Impact of Social Investing on Charitable Donations
authors: Jake An; Donnel A. Briley; Shai Danziger; Shai Levi
n_adoption_cohorts_note: One policy date: introduction of the SI fund on the Raiz app in early June 2017 (pre-introduction switch weeks 2017-04-03..2017-05-29, post 2017-06-05..2017-08-21 in Data_for_MS_readers.csv).
eligible_reason: Not a staggered panel design. Each observation is a portfolio-switch event (investor x switch week). The outcome chdonations is the change in the investor's donations around his or her own switch (Delta Donations), and post marks switches after the single introduction date of the SI fund. All pre-introduction switchers are non-SI by construction (post==0 rows: 4,374, all Non-SI), so post_si equals si and the Table V 'difference-in-differences' compares SI switchers with non-SI switchers before and after one fund launch, on event-level change scores with switch-week (sdate) FE. That is a single-date 2x2, not a binary treatment switching on at unit-specific dates. Table V column 1 has no unit FE. Table V column 2 adds investor FE (identified only from investors with several switch events; residual df 2,513) plus logbalance (pre-switch balance, which differs across an investor's switch events), and neither the investor id nor any investor characteristic is shipped.
design_notes: Program for data editor.R (run by the data editor on the full proprietary file ms.csv; output in Program for data editor_outputfile.txt) and Program for MS readers.R (runs on the shipped excerpt Data_for_MS_readers.csv, which has only port6, post, group, chdonations, si, post_si, chdonate, sdate). Table I: group means and t-tests of Delta Donations (SI switchers, other switchers, matched non-switchers). Table II: felm(chdonations ~ si + logbalance + logincome + logage | sdate | 0 | id+sdate) on post-introduction switchers (cross-section, switch-week FE). Table III: means by donation category. Table IV: adds BD (budgets donations, survey) and si x BD (subgroup interaction). Table V col 1: felm(chdonations ~ post_si + logbalance + logincome + logage | sdate), all switchers pre and post introduction; col 2: felm(chdonations ~ post_si + logbalance | id + sdate). Table VI: chdonate / chndonate (change in donation incidence) on post_si with sdate FE. Table VII: adds chreturns (return difference between new and old fund) and prefund FE. The shipped excerpt reproduces the no-controls versions of Tables I, II, V (col 1) and VI (11,852 rows for Table V, matching the published N).

specs.exclusion_reason: single policy date (SI-fund introduction), event-level change-score outcome, no unit FE; time-varying controls (logbalance) in the published column
specs.outcome: chdonations (change in donations around the investor's switch)
specs.sample_condition: port6 != -1 (switchers only, pre and post introduction)
specs.notes: No-controls version (Program for MS readers.R) runs on the shipped excerpt: post_si -0.575 (p=0.015), N=11,852.

specs.exclusion_reason: single policy date; outcome is an event-level change score; logbalance control varies across an investor's switch events; investor id and controls not shipped
specs.notes: Identified from investors with more than one switch event.

data_access_note: Raiz customer data are proprietary (Data readme file.pdf). The package ships an excerpt of the regression sample without investor id and without investor characteristics (balance, income, age, survey answers, returns, prefund).
data_files: Data_for_MS_readers.csv (15,129 switch-event rows; no investor id, no controls)
data_provenance_note: Real data excerpt (row count matches the published Table V N) with identifying and control columns removed; no synthetic or rescaled values.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text; abstract from data/frame/mnsc.jsonl). The paper calls Table V a difference-in-differences analysis, but the pre/post split is a single fund-introduction date and the units are switch events, not a unit panel with staggered adoption.
